questions.question: What does raising the temperature do to the next-token distribution?
options: Flattens it, so less likely tokens are chosen more often
Sharpens it toward the top token
questions.explanation: Scores are divided by the temperature before softmax; dividing by more than 1 shrinks the gaps.

questions.question: With top_p = 0.9, which tokens can be sampled?
options: The smallest set of most likely tokens whose probabilities add up to at least 0.9
questions.explanation: The nucleus adapts: when the model is confident, it may be one or two tokens.

questions.question: Which setting suits an agent's tool-call step?
options: Temperature 0 (or very low): there's one right call
questions.explanation: Randomness in tool selection or JSON only adds failures.

questions.question: In the live run, temperature 0.8 with seed 42 produced how many distinct taglines in 10 runs?
questions.explanation: A seed fixes the random draws, so sampling becomes repeatable while still not greedy.

questions.question: Identical temperature-0 requests returned 89.0976% and 88.8210% for the same token. What caused it?
options: A cached prompt is computed in a different floating-point order than a fresh one
questions.explanation: Fresh runs and cache hits each gave one exact value. Floating-point addition isn't perfectly associative.

questions.question: Why should evals of a temperature-0 agent still run each case several times?
options: Small numerical differences can flip near-tied tokens, so behaviour can vary between runs
questions.explanation: Determinism is best effort. Measure rates, not single runs.
